title: Handle a Backordered Laptop
subtitle: Capture a blocked physical task honestly
scenario: You place the laptop order and get bad news: the standard laptop is backordered, earliest delivery SD+3 - three days AFTER the start. You cannot make it land in time. Capture the handoff honestly as not on track, so the tracker shows blocked and the gate can escalate instead of pretending.
input: Task: hardware for hire H-4022 (owner IT Provisioner, due SD-2). The Standard laptop is backordered; earliest delivery is SD+3, after the start date. It cannot arrive by the deadline. Capture the order truthfully: it is not on track, which marks this branch blocked for the tracker.
instructions: Set the realistic delivery date (the backordered SD+3).
Mark that it is NOT on track for the start.
Validate to mint the (blocked) hardware handoff record.

fields.label: Ordered by

successMessage: Backorder captured honestly. The branch is blocked - the gate can now escalate instead of assuming.

intro.heading: When a physical task cannot make it

sections.title: Honesty over optimism
sections.body: The worst thing to do with a backorder is record a hopeful date. The tracker and the gate act on what you write; a rosy delivery date turns into a hire with no laptop on day one.

sections.title: Blocked is a real state
sections.body: Marking not-on-track sets this branch to blocked. That is not a failure of the workflow - it is the workflow doing its job, surfacing a problem while there is still time to act.

sections.title: The gate needs the truth
sections.body: A blocked branch is exactly what the readiness gate is built to catch. Capturing it truthfully is what routes the hire to escalation instead of a silent miss.

sections.title: What you produce here
sections.body: A blocked hardware record with a reason. The tracker will show it blocked, and escalation will arrange a loaner.

realWorld.soloRebuildPath: You'd record the real backorder date and flag it, rather than writing a delivery date you hope comes true.
